items.title: Ellis Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: recommending a friend of mine who had been the sister of my first piano teacher, Antoinette Miller

ctx.x: How did that position come about?

I was disillusioned – no, I was disenchanted with the situation at New Orleans Center for Creative Arts, because I didn’t have students that I needed to keep going the way we were functioning, because it was a high-end program. It was not some of those jazz programs where they spend all of their time teaching you rock-and-roll and call it jazz. It was not that. I didn’t have any students. So I was telling my wife. I said, “I’m tired of this. I don’t want to do this no more, because I don’t have the students that…
a classical flautist. She wrote a book on – her mentor was – what’s this woman’s name? She wrote this book on African-American music.
